items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Dick Wilson, who was a fine tenor saxaphone player, he's a stylist, actually, and he was with Zack White.

ctx.x: Nate Toles. Because we were together and he had like six pieces when John Hammond heard them coming from the Reno Club and things. But he quickly got his band together. But it was said that I said the Nat Toles band was better all throughout than Basie's band, which they weren't. You know, I didn't mean that. But we had a hell of a band.

So I -- oh, I'm a little ahead of my story. While I'm in Wylie, Andy Kirk's band, they hoboed back to Kansas City and Dick Wilson, who was a fine tenor saxaphone player, he's a stylist, actually, and he was with Zack White. But Andy called me, he sent three telegrams and says, "Look, we're going to record. The band's back together and I think we're going to make it." He says, "A guy coming down from Decca is going to record us and I want you to be on it."

So by this time, Gary, I didn't want to go through no more hard times. I was having a nice time there, you know. I just didn't go and I didn't regret it because later, I ended up with Basie, you know. But sure enough, they recorded "Until the Real Thing Comes Along." That was their big song, you know, with --
